objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the low-temperature annealing chamber in reducing the calibration drift of the pressure sensor.
dependent_variables: calibration drift of the pressure sensor
baseline: Calibration drift of the same pressure sensor without the low-temperature annealing chamber
procedure: Step 1: Prepare the pressure sensor and the low-temperature annealing chamber according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Step 2: Set up the control unit to interact with the pressure sensor and the low-temperature annealing chamber.
Step 3: Operate the device under a constant pressure of 1000 mbar for 30 days.
Step 4: Apply a thermal treatment every 24 hours for 1 hour at a temperature of 150°C using the low-temperature annealing chamber.
Step 5: Measure the calibration drift of the pressure sensor at regular intervals over the 30-day period.
expected_result: A 30% reduction in the calibration drift of the pressure sensor over a period of 30 days.
falsification_condition: If the calibration drift of the pressure sensor with the low-temperature annealing chamber is not significantly lower than the calibration drift of the same pressure sensor without the low-temperature annealing chamber after 30 days of operation.
sample_requirements: A minimum of 5 identical pressure sensors and 5 identical low-temperature annealing chambers are required for this experiment.
safety_constraints: The experiment must be conducted in a well-ventilated area, and the device must be operated at a safe distance from any flammable materials.
information_gain: The experiment will provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of the low-temperature annealing chamber in reducing the calibration drift of the pressure sensor, which can be used to improve the design and operation of similar devices.
